items.title: FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang
items.summary: GYIRONG, Xizang, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- Rescue operations intensified Thursday at the mudslide-stricken border port of Gyirong in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, as rescue teams and helicopters were dispatched to the disaster area. The first team of 141 rescuers arrived at the port on Thursday morning after the disaster caused significant casualties along the China-Nepal border, according to China's Ministry of Emergency Management.

items.title: NDRRMA rescue coordination portal
items.summary: NDRRMA publishes rescue and coordination updates for the Bhotekoshi / Rasuwa flash flood on its official rescue portal and the SETU platform (setu.ndrrma.gov.np). Families should use these official channels for status — not unofficial social media reposts. This site links to NDRRMA; we do not copy individual case data.

items.title: Nepal Police official found and missing lists
items.summary: Nepal Police maintains the official Unified Database for missing persons, found persons, and unidentified remains related to the flood-affected areas. Search at udb.nepalpolice.gov.np/missing and udb.nepalpolice.gov.np/found. Official confirmation of status comes only from Nepal Police — not from volunteer sites or social media.

items.title: Embassy of India, Kathmandu — assistance for Indian nationals
items.summary: The Embassy of India in Kathmandu is coordinating with Nepalese authorities on search and rescue for Indian nationals affected by flash floods in the Rasuwa / Bhotekoshi area. Indian nationals and families may also contact the MEA Special Control Room in Delhi: +91-11-23088718, +91-11-23088719, WhatsApp +91-9968291988, email situationroom@mea.gov.in. Embassy WhatsApp: +977-9851316807.

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026
items.summary: So far, 72 bodies have been recovered, while many people are still feared missing. According to the latest available information, 403 people from 25 countries, including Nepal, have been reported missing- 203 males and 200 females. Of these, 62 are Nepali nationals and 341 are foreign nationals. These figures remain subject to verification as search and rescue operations continue.
